minutes.headline: Zoning board approved two special permits: a rebuild at 56 Pine Street and a land transfer at 27 The Clearing.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals held two remote hearings. The first was a special permit to demolish and rebuild a single-family home on a non-conforming lot at 56 Pine Street. The second was a special permit to convey a small parcel with a garage between neighbouring lots on The Clearing. Both were announced as approved after roll calls, and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked about land grading and water runoff from the septic tank and leaching field toward his property.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit to demolish and rebuild the dwelling at 56 Pine Street as requested.
Approve the special permit for the land transfer from the Dobys to the Coopers at The Clearing.

decisions.decision: Special permit granted for 56 Pine Street with compliance conditions, including the Board of Health conditions; must be recorded at the registry and lapses in two years without substantial use.
Special permit granted for the land conveyance at 27 The Clearing with the standard compliance contingency; must be recorded and lapses in two years.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a special permit to demolish and rebuild the house at 56 Pine Street, on a roll call vote.
The 56 Pine Street permit carries compliance conditions, including Board of Health conditions, and lapses in two years without substantial use.
The board approved a special permit for a land transfer between neighbouring lots at 27 The Clearing, on a roll call vote.
The Clearing permit carries the standard compliance contingency, must be recorded, and lapses in two years.
A resident asked about grading and water runoff from the septic tank and leaching field toward his property during the Pine Street hearing.

why_it_matters: A rebuild on a non-conforming lot and a shift in lot lines change what can be built next door, so abutters' drainage and setback concerns are settled at this stage, in the permit conditions.
Both permits must be recorded at the registry and lapse in two years if unused, which sets the window for the work to begin.
